original_card.question: Can one measured replay bottleneck be sped up without dropping coverage?
methods: Profile one isolated replay and optimize the measured bottleneck.
Design source-bound reuse with explicit dependency invalidation and negative controls.
original_card.acceptance_gate: Report before/after wall time on the same fixture, retained checks and invalidation behavior.

first_step.inspect: Read the selected reproduction command and choose a single replay stage for profiling.
first_step.scope: Positive control / source-bound orientation only; this is not a new construction or full cold replay.

original_card.first_experiment: Measure one unchanged fixture, preserve check coverage, and test one optimization with invalidation controls.
original_card.bottleneck_link: Faster trustworthy replays increase review throughput and let mechanism candidates be checked sooner.
allowed_variations: Profile one stage or design one source-bound cache boundary.
scope_change_triggers: Skipping coverage or comparing different fixtures to claim speedup.

actual_scope: Can scripts/exclusion_circuit.py:ExclusionCircuit.verify replace its leave-two-out expected-support genexpr with an equivalent closed-form pair mask (full ^ (vertex[a]|vertex[b])) so verify receipts, circuit_sha256 and support assertions stay fieldwise identical on the historical n=45 circuit?
scope_change_reason: The catalogue card asks for one measured replay bottleneck with before/after wall time and retained checks. Expertise override selected verifier-engineering after open tooling PR #1994 left ExclusionCircuit.verify's leave-two-out expected-support genexpr as an explicit next question. Profiling named that genexpr (not the single json.dumps) as the verify hot path.
bottleneck_link: Side result on review throughput: shared-point verify, bit-compression and several historical side-circuit certificates call ExclusionCircuit.verify. A faster identical support check does not change kappa or the binding complex supplier.
stop_rule: Ship an equivalence-preserving ExclusionCircuit.verify support-mask change with frozen baseline, identical receipts on the historical n=45 circuit, updated source pins only on the four binding certificates, registered replay and a measured before/after median. Do not reopen mathematical screens, rewrite SharedPointCircuit digests, or run the selected cold frontier replay.
evidence: PASS_EXCLUSION_SUPPORT_MASKS via research/exclusion-support-masks/verify.py (also under -O); PASS_IDENTICAL_EXCLUSION_SUPPORT_MASK_RECEIPTS via benchmark.py; four certificates differ from base only in the scripts/exclusion_circuit.py source pin.
author: Wentao Li
ai_assistance: Substantial AI assistance for orientation, overlap search, profiling, implementation, packaging, benchmarking and writing. Not independent human peer review.

open_questions.question: Should research/bit-compression-provenance and other packages that pin live scripts/exclusion_circuit.py bytes refresh those SHA-256 entries after this equivalence-preserving rewrite?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Those provenance packages bind working-tree bytes; leaving the old pin keeps this tooling PR focused, but a later full provenance replay on main would see a hash mismatch until refreshed.
open_questions.first_step: Open a dedicated provenance follow-up that only rewrites the exclusion_circuit.py entry in those SOURCES/SOURCE-PINS files after confirming circuit_sha256 identity.
open_questions.blocked_by: Pin repair outside the four binding certificates is outside this tooling change.

open_questions.question: Is ExclusionCircuit.verify_embedding's reverse-frame expected-support sum worth a separate identical-receipt rewrite?
open_questions.why_it_matters: verify_embedding uses a similar leave-two style genexpr for reverse frames; it is a different object from the verify leave-two-out path measured here.
open_questions.first_step: Profile ExclusionCircuit(45).verify_embedding alone and check whether a closed-form reverse mask matches the historical expected bits.
open_questions.blocked_by: Out of this session's stop rule; ExclusionCircuit.verify support masks were the measured bottleneck left by #1994.
